dedupe_keys.name: wapa neutral blocking device against geomagnetically induced currents at white substation south dakota

description: This WAPA article (April 2023) describes the first commercially developed neutral blocking device in the United States, installed in the neutral of large power transformer KU1A at White Substation, South Dakota, to block geomagnetically induced currents during solar storms. Funded by the Department of Energy's Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security and Emergency Response as a national pilot, it followed an EPRI GIC mitigation pilot report and two studies: a GIC flow study in which Upper Great Plains planners simulated storms of varying orientation and magnitude and trial device placements at key nodes, choosing White because it links three or more substations with large transformers on long 345 kV lines, and an impact study of transient switching, harmonics and insulation that found no negative effects. The device, bought from Emprimus, keeps a grounded metallic path and switches neutral current through a capacitor bank above a GIC threshold, with a spark gap for overvoltage. It was delivered in September 2022 and energised in November 2022, and during the G3 storm of 27 February 2023 it operated as expected four times over about twelve hours. The article is accessible online as free HTML on wapa.gov. Caveats: it is a utility news feature, and the study reports are not published there. It illustrates simulation-based placement of space weather mitigation for grid resilience; related records are NOAA SWPC products and SuperMAG.
